items.title: ‘Incredibly unusual’ bird migrating from Siberia found in Cumbria – killed by cat

items.title: A global Microsoft 365 outage has hit millions – what happened and when will it be fixed?
items.desc: Problem affects businesses, government agencies and even tech firm’s own employees Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook Microsoft outage – live updates Tell us: have you been affected by the Microsoft outage? Millions of people were unable to access their emails, Teams chats or meetings on Thursday night and Friday morning after a Microsoft 365 outage brought down services across the globe. The incident affected businesses, government agencies and even Microsoft employees. Businesses, government agencies and vital services around the world have all reported issues, from the US House of Representatives to an Australian spy agency and airlines in India. In the UK, police services, ambulances and hospitals reported issues with email services and online form submissions. Continue reading...

The sprawling five-hectare (13-acre) campus, which hosted just 650 workers when it opened in 1986, has solidified Dorset’s status as one of Britain’s largest financial hubs outside London. items.title: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor leaves band due to tinnitus
items.desc: ‘I must now listen to my body and my doctors’, says Taylor, who was one of the earliest members of the new wave hit-makers The drummer for Duran Duran, Roger Taylor, is to step down from the band due to worsening tinnitus. In a statement, Taylor said: “This is one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever had to make. Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I’ve reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors.” Continue reading...
